cases.title: PM CARES: identify agency refunds before tracing onward money
cases.question: Which agencies returned FY 2024–25 funds, and what happened to each original allotment?
cases.finding: The latest listed statement reports ₹324.66 crore of agency refunds and only ₹87.85 lakh of cash payments, but omits the referenced notes identifying agencies and projects. Those gaps stop the money trace; they do not establish theft.

geography.label: New Delhi

geography.label: Bengaluru
geography.basis: BEL corporate-disclosure association, not evidence of contract influence

claims.text: Downloaded FY 2024–25 one-page statement references note 11 for agency refunds and notes 1–16/auditor report, which are not included in that PDF.
claims.response: FAQ says an independent auditor audits the fund and says no statutory Income Tax audit period is prescribed.
claims.alternative: Ordinary explanation: unused advances or settled excess allotments returned; notes may exist internally. Data alternative: publication/linking omission or different document version.
claims.falsifier: Obtain signed note 11 and agency-wise refund advices; reconcile original release, expenditure, interest and return to bank records.
missingRecords: Agency/project refund schedule and return vouchers

claims.text: A reported BEL CSR donation is a documented contribution, not evidence that procurement awards were purchased.
claims.response: BEL states pandemic-relief purpose; FAQ allows CSR contributions.
claims.alternative: CSR compliance and emergency assistance explain donation without an improper agreement.
claims.falsifier: An influence allegation requires dated decision communications, tender evaluation and an independently matched transfer; shared entity or timing alone is nondiagnostic.
missingRecords: Any specifically alleged procurement decision file

claims.text: January 2026 reporting describes oral RTI privacy observations; a later final disposition was not verified in this research.
claims.response: Article reports appeal from 22 January 2024 single-judge decision and adjournment.
claims.alternative: Third-party procedural protections may explain nondisclosure; they do not determine the truth of procurement allegations.
claims.falsifier: Read certified latest docket and final order before describing RTI legal status as settled.
missingRecords: Latest appeal docket and signed orders

FY 2022–23 separately identifies a ₹202.89 crore ventilator-programme refund; FY 2024–25 does not identify the agency.
FY 2024–25 closing balance ₹8,452.07 crore is a stock; incoming agency refunds recycle prior disbursements and are not new donations.

Donor-level fund receipts and resulting end-use beyond available aggregate disclosures.

cases.title: Bihar PM-JAY: two procurement clusters, one administrator
cases.question: Why did both clusters go to one TPA at different rates despite NHA advice, and how were penalties and payments reconciled?
cases.finding: CAG reports both 2023 clusters awarded to Family Health Plan Insurance TPA at ₹1.95/₹1.68 per family-year, ₹1.19 crore paid, and an estimated ₹8.80 lakh avoidable component. Bihar cites procurement-rule and staffing differences; CAG rejects that explanation.

geography.label: Patna
geography.basis: BSSS procurement/administration association; no inferred private-bank coordinates

claims.text: CAG §1.7.2 describes deviation from NHA advice against allocating both clusters to one bidder and against unequal rates.
claims.response: BSSS November 2024 reply: L2-to-L1 matching would be negotiation not recommended by Bihar Financial Rules; different district counts required different staffing. CAG says family counts/nature of work were nearly same.
claims.alternative: Ordinary explanation: distinct cluster staffing costs and legal concern about post-bid negotiations. Error alternative: the final RFP could differ from the draft guidance or table-period scope.
claims.falsifier: Obtain operative RFP, NHA correspondence, comparative bid schedule and rule opinion. A lawful documented deviation and cost model could narrow or overturn the audit concern.

claims.text: ₹8.80 lakh is CAG’s estimated avoidable component of payment, not a separate transfer or bribe.
claims.response: CAG footnote 23 computes family count×rate difference×half-year, less 10% penalty, plus 18% GST; gross payments include tax withholding.
claims.alternative: Difference may reflect permitted staffing/service variation; gross deduction-based amount may differ from bank receipt.
claims.falsifier: Recompute from invoices, service periods, family denominator, GST/TDS and penalty ledgers; establish actual net paid.

claims.text: CAG criticises earlier Medsave contract scope and later Vidal deployment gaps; these are distinct contracts, not proof the three TPAs shared owners or coordinated.
claims.response: BSSS defended hospital-based ISA scope in 2022; in November 2024 reported 359 PMAMs deployed by September 2024 and ordered remaining deployment.
claims.alternative: Interpretation differences and staffing rollout can explain part of the shortfall; contract-performance gaps require specific invoice/attendance checks.
claims.falsifier: Compare signed clauses, staffing rosters and approved deductions separately for each agency.
missingRecords: Vidal 2022 agreement, rosters and payment deductions

whatWeKnow: CAG gives a reproducible ₹879,882 calculation, rounded ₹8.80 lakh.
Bihar PM-JAY operates in assurance/trust mode; TPAs administer claims rather than underwriting all hospital expenditure.
Agency amounts and hospital claims belong to distinct payment populations.
whatWeDoNotKnow: Final legal opinion on rule conflict, bidders’ identities/ranks, all contract amendments, net agency receipt and later recoveries.
No ownership or political-connection evidence was inspected for the TPAs.
